questions.text: Does the document explicitly encourage building local capacity across council, their local communities and neighbouring local councils for climate action?
questions.answer: The document does explicitly encourage building local capacity across council, their local communities, and neighbouring local councils for climate action. It mentions the Cities Power Partnership (CPP), an initiative of the Climate Council, which represents Australia’s largest local government climate action network. The CPP encourages local councils to make five action pledges in either renewable energy, efficiency, transport, or working in partnership to tackle climate change. The partnership also facilitates connection and sharing between participants, providing a platform for councils to learn from each other's experiences and initiatives. Furthermore, the document suggests that councils consider joining groups such as the Business Renewables Centre – Australia (BRC-A) and engaging with other councils in their region and with some who have signed Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs). This indicates an advocacy for collaboration and capacity building among local councils.
